Trinity Health IHA Medical Group is seeking a compassionate and patient-focused Behavioral Health Specialist

Job Description

The Crisis Call Diversion Program/Deflection exists to deflect nonviolent behavioral health calls from 911 to a team of behavioral health providers that respond over the phone and in the community to meet the person in crisis where they are and connect to ongoing resources and support.

Schedule may include overnight hours.

Oversees day-to-day operations of the Deflection program. Creates and maintains staff work schedules, including requests for time off. Provide staffing of runs to determine appropriate intervention and level of care during the crisis. Ensure team is fully assessing each crisis, providing an appropriate level of care, and follow-up throughout the individual’s time of crisis as determined by person in crisis. Ensure continuous quality improvement of Deflection program by monitoring flow from initial call through release from case manager. Ensure team is working collaboratively with law enforcement, families, other county departments, schools, acute care services providers, and other community resources to coordinate appropriate crisis resolution and referral. Ensure team is communicating pertinent information on a timely basis to persons in crisis, MetroSafe call takers and dispatch, LMPD, SCS, and any other appropriate parties while also preserving the dignity and privacy of the person in crisis as much as possible. Ensure team is completing and coordinating accurate, timely, and thorough documentation of all interventions transacted during the work shift. Assist with initial and ongoing training needs of the team. Perform other duties as assigned to assist Unit Manager. Be reasonably available to respond to emergency coverage needs. Facilitate a culture of openness and collaboration to ensure all team members are providing accurate, quality, crisis assistance, including accurate documentation. Attend, participate, and be available to lead weekly team meetings. Utilize person centered and trauma informed approach to each interaction.

The intent of this job description is to provide a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this job. Incumbents may be requested to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically presented in this description.

EDUCATION

Bachelor’s Degree.
Master's degree Sociology, Social Work, Psychology, Special Education, Human Services, or a related field of study (preferred)

Experience

Over four years human/social services experience with a supervisory background, and experience with program management.
Thorough knowledge of relevant client population characteristics and related crisis response interventions.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Good interpersonal skills.
Good public speaking abilities.
Thorough knowledge of Deflection model and program contract deliverables.
Good supervisory skills.

Physical Demands/Requirements

Position requires lifting of 20 pounds maximum, with frequent lifting and/or carrying of items weighing up to 10 pounds or requires significant periods of walking or standing.
Exposure to threat of bodily harm from clients or families, or unpleasant situations such as offensive language from callers.
Normal tasks may involve exposure to blood, bodily fluids, or tissue.
May involve 24-hour on-call responsibilities.
Ability to work a flexible schedule including evenings and weekends.
Valid driver's license required, and met criteria to drive SCS-owned vehicles.
Must meet all work and background check requirements for the MetroSafe call center.

Position Title

Job Description Summary

The Regional Hub Program Coordinator provides operational and administrative support for the Thrive Kansas Digital Mental Health Initiative within an assigned Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) regional hub. This position coordinates day-to-day implementation activities, training and onboarding logistics, meeting and communication activities, documentation and record management, and project tracking. The role serves as a key resource for participating sites, community health workers (CHWs), providers, implementation partners, and regional leadership, helping ensure regional activities are completed efficiently, consistently, and in alignment with project timelines, reporting requirements, and continuous quality improvement (CQI) processes.

The Thrive Kansas Digital Mental Health Initiative is a grant funded, statewide, evidence-based digital therapeutic strategy designed to expand access to treatment for depression, substance use disorders (SUD) and other mental disorders in rural Kansas. The initiative deploys clinically validated computerized mental health interventions supported by community-based facilitation and integrated into rural primary care, behavioral health, and community settings.

We are currently recruiting for three program coordinator positions.

Job Description

Job Duties

Regional Deployment & Site Coordination

Track completion of regional onboarding, deployment, and access setup activities for participating sites. Maintain deployment task lists, implementation documentation, and project records.
Schedule and coordinate deployment-related meetings and communications. Log, monitor, and route technical issues to appropriate project personnel and track issue resolution.
Maintain records related to deployment activities, onboarding progress, implementation milestones, and site readiness.
Support the Regional Hub Program Manager in monitoring implementation progress, identifying potential barriers, and facilitating successful deployment activities.

Training Coordination & Implementation Support

Schedule and coordinate regional training sessions for providers, CHWs, supervisors, navigators, and program staff. Track training attendance, completion, certifications, and related documentation. Distribute training materials, reminders, schedules, and follow-up communications. Serve as the first point of contact for routine implementation questions and assist with resolving common operational concerns.
Support onboarding and implementation activities for participating sites, organizations, and staff. Coordinate logistics and facilitate stakeholder communication to support successful adoption of digital mental health services.

Workforce & Program Operations Support

Support onboarding logistics for CHWs, case management staff, and other program personnel. Maintain regional staffing rosters, contact lists, distribution lists, and workforce documentation.
Coordinate routine communication among CHWs, supervisors, project staff, and participating organizations, and track operational issues and implementation barriers affecting program activities.
Document workflow modifications, process updates, and operational improvements to help ensure consistency across participating sites and regional partners.

Evaluation, Reporting & Continuous Quality Improvement

Track regional data submission schedules, reporting deadlines, and project deliverables. Coordinate meetings associated with evaluation activities, reporting reviews, and CQI initiatives.
Document meeting notes, action items, decisions, and follow-up tasks, and maintain records for grant administration, reporting, and project documentation.
Support preparation and dissemination of summaries, reports, presentations, slide decks, and stakeholder communications.
Assist the Regional Hub Program Manager in monitoring completion of CQI action items and reporting requirements.

User Support & Access Coordination

Coordinate logistics associated with participant, provider, and stakeholder support activities. Track access-related issues reported by users, CHWs, providers, and participating sites.
Route user access concerns to the appropriate technical or program staff and monitor progress toward resolution. Maintain user-facing support materials, frequently asked questions (FAQs), reference guides, and communication resources.
Track recurring access barriers and support identification of trends that require escalation to regional leadership or project management teams.

Support communication among participating healthcare organizations, community partners, providers, and project teams within the regional hub.
Coordinate meeting logistics, maintain distribution lists, prepare communications, and facilitate follow-up activities related to project implementation.
Assist in maintaining positive relationships with participating organizations and stakeholders.
Support dissemination of project updates, training opportunities, implementation resources, and program information throughout the region.

Integration with Regional & Statewide Program Operations

Maintain documentation, records, and communications that support coordination across regional hubs and statewide leadership teams.
Participate in statewide coordination meetings, implementation activities, and quality improvement initiatives as assigned.
Assist in sharing lessons learned, implementation best practices, and operational insights across project teams and partner organizations.

TITLE: Program Coordinator

FLSA CLASSIFICATION: Exempt

HOURS: Full-time

RESPONSIBLE TO: St. Louis City Director

DIRECT REPORTS: St. Lazare House Staff

LOCATION: St. Louis, MO

SALARY: $55,000-$60,000 per year, paid bi-weekly

Mission

Depaul USA supports homeless and marginalized people, providing people experiencing homelessness with purpose and hope for a positive future. Our vision is that everyone has a place to call home and a stake in his or her community. In cities across the nation, we meet people where they are to address their needs. Through a combination of homelessness services and housing, Depaul USA is innovating and bringing real solutions to those facing homelessness.

Depaul USA Is a Growing, National, Not-for-profit Organization That Serves More Than 7,000 People Annually And Has a Combined Operating And Capital Budget In Excess Of $12.5 Million. Our Vincentian Values Underpin What We Do

We celebrate the potential of people;
We put our words into action;
We aim to take a wider role in civil society; and
We believe in rights and responsibilities.

Please visit www.depaulusa.org to learn more.

Depaul USA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace, and we are firmly committed to creating an equitable and inclusive environment for all employees. If you need reasonable accommodation in any part of the hiring process, please let us know.

Position Description

The Program Coordinator will oversee and manage St. Lazare House, ensuring that clients receive the appropriate support, resources, and services to help them achieve long-term stability. Responsibilities include client outreach, eligibility screening, counseling, and coordinating housing and services in compliance with HUD guidelines. The Program Coordinator will manage documentation, reports, and ensure clients are connected to resources and maintain progress toward permanent housing. Additionally, the position includes supervising staff and collaborating with service providers to support client needs, while reporting to and working closely with the St. Louis City Director.

Primary Duties And Responsibilities

Essential Functions

Set policy and programming to ensure that clients are getting the support that they need and that all guidelines are followed as outlined by Grantors and other funders
Outreach/screen potential clients for eligibility using the Coordinated Entry Front Door for all referrals
Welcome new clients, educate them on program guidelines, and provide counseling to assist with lease understanding, utility setup, and movingin process.
Mediate conflicts or issues between tenants and/or between tenants and staff in a constructive and empathetic manner, fostering a safe and respectful environment for all participants.
Ensure ongoing compliance with HUD guidelines for PSH rental assistance programs
Ensure timely submission of required reports and documentation to remain in grant compliance (e.g., monthly activity and finance reports, Annual Progress Report, grant renewals).
Ensure client charts include required eligibility documents, progress notes, treatment plans, and other necessary paperwork
Work with maintenance to fix identified problems prior to clients movein and while clients reside in units
Conduct a psychosocial and needs assessment with each client at entry
Develop with clients at entry and yearly thereafter an individualized housing and service plan, including planning a path to permanent housing
Provide individual and group counseling to help clients improve quality of life, support clients in addressing behaviors and building skills for stable housing and develop healthier coping strategies
Provide medication education and management
Assist clients in obtaining and maintaining eligible benefits, seeking job training, improving job skills, pursuing education (e.g., GED), and finding employment
Connect clients to community resources and supports and encourage ongoing participation
Coordinate care with other service providers and involved supports
Manages Human Resources tasks promptly, including payroll submissions to the Director of HR, interviewing, onboarding, coaching, training, and development of all staff and volunteers.

Additional Tasks and Responsibilities

Supervise life coach and all house monitor staff to ensure the use of good clinical care and respectful treatment of all clients
Provide a means of communication that clients and staff may use 24/7 for emergencies
Provide crisis intervention as needed
Maintains all relevant program information current in both paper and electronic formats
Develop programming as needed to better meet the everchanging need of the clients
Provide transportation to clients as needed to achieve goals
Enter and update client data in HMIS and the New Org database weekly, with annual updates as required. Use data to assess program effectiveness and contribute to evaluation reports
Attend community meetings, network with other service providers, and advocate for the homeless within the St. Louis City CoC
Recruit, orient, and supervise Depaul USA volunteers and practicum students to support the program’s operations and enhance service delivery for clients.
Work closely with Depaul USA grant writer, accountant and bookkeeper to ensure good practices, grant renewal and help to secure financial stability for the ongoing needs of the program

General Responsibilities

Adhere to all quality assurance policies and procedures.
Stay informed of current local and national events, trends, and issues, that impact Depaul USA’s work with homeless individuals.
Strive continuously to develop the role in collaboration with the supervisor to ensure that all tasks are being undertaken in an effective and appropriate manner, meeting the strategic goals and objectives of Depaul USA.
Participate in internal/external meetings as required, attends training events, conferences, and other functions as necessary.
Participate in regular supervision and annual evaluations, identifying his or her own developmental and training needs.
Ensure adherence to all Depaul USA policies and procedures, particularly those relating to Health and Safety, Safeguarding and the Code of Practice and Confidentiality.
Contribute to the effective implementation of Depaul USA’s Equal Opportunities Policy as it affects both the organization and its work with this client group.
Undertake the role in a professional manner maintaining a highquality standard of work, in accordance with the Vision, Mission and Values of Depaul USA.

Qualifications

The Ideal Program Coordinator Will Be a Professional With At Least Five Years Of Experience In Case Management With Vulnerable Segments Of The Population. S/he Will Have Experience Working With Individuals Who Have Faced Homelessness And Struggled With Issues Of Mental Illness, Cognitive Disabilities, And Addictions, As Well People Who Are Newly Housed Or Employed. The Program Coordinator Should Possess The Following

Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in related field (ex. social work, psychology, etc.); 5 years’ work experience in related field; Licensed Clinical Social Worker preferred.
Exceptional communication, multi‐tasking, conflict management and interpersonal skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), and experience with data management systems
Ability to organize tasks, events, people, and delegate effectively.
Ability to exercise independent judgment when appropriate and strong decisionmaking skills.
Experience working with diverse populations

Work Schedule:

Onsite at St. Lazare House, 2912 Arsenal St, St. Louis, MO with limited offsite work.
Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM CST.
In rotation with leadership team on call evenings, nights, weekends and holidays

Company provided Basic Life/AD&D & Short/Long Term disability policies.
401(k) Retirement plan with employer match.
Generous Vacation, Sick, and Personal leave and 10 Observed holidays.

Description

MiFamily Together Advocate - Social Worker

Shiawassee and Gratiot counties | Hybrid - Wellspring Lansing | $48,000 / year | Accepting applications until August 14, 2026.

Help families stay together. Help them move forward.

Most people choose a career in human services because they believe people can grow. They believe families can overcome challenges. They believe children deserve the opportunity to thrive in safe, stable, and supportive environments.

The MFT Advocate - Social Worker role is an opportunity to put those beliefs into action every day.

As part of Michigan’s MiFamily Together program with Wellspring, you'll work alongside families who are navigating some of life's most difficult moments. MiFamily Together was designed to help preserve families, reduce unnecessary out-of-home placements, support reunification, and strengthen family well-being through a coordinated, whole-family approach. Rather than asking families to navigate multiple disconnected services, the program focuses on building trusting relationships, addressing the needs of both children and caregivers, and helping families create lasting stability and success.

As an MFT Advocate, you will serve as a guide, partner, teacher, coach and source of support for families facing a variety of challenges. Whether a family is working through housing instability, mental health concerns, substance use issues, parenting struggles, financial hardship or child welfare involvement, your role is to help them identify strengths, build skills, access resources and move toward their goals.

This is relationship-based work. It is the opportunity to meet families where they are, listen without judgment, recognize strengths that may have been overlooked, and help create pathways toward long-term safety and well-being.

The impact of this work extends far beyond a single family.

When parents gain confidence, children benefit. When families become more stable, communities become stronger. When protective factors increase, the likelihood of abuse and neglect decreases. Through your work, you will help create positive outcomes that can influence generations to come.

What You'll Do

As an Advocate, your work centers around four key areas:

Building trusting relationships. You will establish meaningful partnerships with families, helping them identify goals, navigate challenges and build on their existing strengths through a respectful, strength-based approach.

Strengthening family safety and stability. You will work alongside caregivers to enhance protective factors, develop plans that address safety concerns, build parenting and life skills, and support families in creating stable environments where children can thrive

Connecting families to resources and opportunities. You will help families access services and supports that address immediate needs while promoting long-term self-sufficiency, including community resources, healthcare, education, housing, transportation, and public benefits.

Collaborating for lasting change. You will partner with schools, healthcare providers, child welfare professionals, referral sources, and community agencies to ensure families receive coordinated and effective support that promotes positive outcomes long after services end.

Who Thrives In This Role

Successful MFT Advocates are compassionate, adaptable and resilient. They are skilled at building rapport with diverse families, maintaining professional boundaries and remaining calm during challenging situations. They are comfortable balancing independence and collaboration, managing changing priorities, and working creatively to help families achieve their goals.

Most importantly, they never lose sight of why they entered this field in the first place: to support people, strengthen families and improve outcomes for children.

Education

Bachelor's degree in social work, psychology, education, or human services related field OR
An associate's degree with two years of experience working with families is acceptable, provided you are actively working toward a bachelor's degree in human services, social work, education or related field and are to be completed with your degree within six months.

Experience

Experience working with children and families.
Familiarity with child welfare systems, community resources, and protective factors frameworks.

What You'll Bring

You believe in the strength and potential of families—even during difficult circumstances. You are skilled at building trust, engaging people from diverse backgrounds, and helping families navigate challenges while maintaining dignity and hope. You bring knowledge of child welfare and community resources, strong organizational and communication skills, and a willingness to adapt to the needs of families.

Applicants must meet all position requirements, including required screenings, driver's license and car insurance requirements, technology expectations, and the ability to maintain a flexible schedule that supports family needs. Preference will be given to applicants who reside within the assigned service area.

Work Environment

This position involves a combination of work performed from a home office or other designated workspace, along with in-home visits and community outreach. The MFT Advocate travels throughout the assigned service area (Shiawassee and Gratiot counties) with mileage paid, including extended travel for multi-county contracts.

Because families are best served where they live and interact, advocates work in a variety of home and community environments that may include animals, smoke, strong odors, clutter, and insects. Evening, weekend and holiday availability is required in order to consistently meet with families and work with their schedules; you'll have supervisor and team support to manage schedules. The role is subject to frequent interruptions, schedule changes based on family needs and driving in all weather conditions.

Why Join Wellspring?

This role is more than a job. It is an opportunity to help families remain safely together, support parents in creating brighter futures for their children, and be part of a program that is transforming the way services are delivered across Michigan. Every conversation, every visit and every relationship has the potential to create lasting change.

If you believe families deserve hope, support and the opportunity to succeed, this role offers the chance to make a meaningful difference every day.

Apply Today.

Description

MiFamily Together Advocate - Social Worker

Shiawassee and Gratiot counties | Hybrid - Wellspring Lansing | $48,000 / year | Accepting applications until August 14, 2026.

Help families stay together. Help them move forward.

Most people choose a career in human services because they believe people can grow. They believe families can overcome challenges. They believe children deserve the opportunity to thrive in safe, stable, and supportive environments.

The MFT Advocate - Social Worker role is an opportunity to put those beliefs into action every day.

As part of Michigan’s MiFamily Together program with Wellspring, you'll work alongside families who are navigating some of life's most difficult moments. MiFamily Together was designed to help preserve families, reduce unnecessary out-of-home placements, support reunification, and strengthen family well-being through a coordinated, whole-family approach. Rather than asking families to navigate multiple disconnected services, the program focuses on building trusting relationships, addressing the needs of both children and caregivers, and helping families create lasting stability and success.

As an MFT Advocate, you will serve as a guide, partner, teacher, coach and source of support for families facing a variety of challenges. Whether a family is working through housing instability, mental health concerns, substance use issues, parenting struggles, financial hardship or child welfare involvement, your role is to help them identify strengths, build skills, access resources and move toward their goals.

This is relationship-based work. It is the opportunity to meet families where they are, listen without judgment, recognize strengths that may have been overlooked, and help create pathways toward long-term safety and well-being.

The impact of this work extends far beyond a single family.

When parents gain confidence, children benefit. When families become more stable, communities become stronger. When protective factors increase, the likelihood of abuse and neglect decreases. Through your work, you will help create positive outcomes that can influence generations to come.

What You'll Do

As an Advocate, your work centers around four key areas:

Building trusting relationships. You will establish meaningful partnerships with families, helping them identify goals, navigate challenges and build on their existing strengths through a respectful, strength-based approach.

Strengthening family safety and stability. You will work alongside caregivers to enhance protective factors, develop plans that address safety concerns, build parenting and life skills, and support families in creating stable environments where children can thrive

Connecting families to resources and opportunities. You will help families access services and supports that address immediate needs while promoting long-term self-sufficiency, including community resources, healthcare, education, housing, transportation, and public benefits.

Collaborating for lasting change. You will partner with schools, healthcare providers, child welfare professionals, referral sources, and community agencies to ensure families receive coordinated and effective support that promotes positive outcomes long after services end.

Who Thrives In This Role

Successful MFT Advocates are compassionate, adaptable and resilient. They are skilled at building rapport with diverse families, maintaining professional boundaries and remaining calm during challenging situations. They are comfortable balancing independence and collaboration, managing changing priorities, and working creatively to help families achieve their goals.

Most importantly, they never lose sight of why they entered this field in the first place: to support people, strengthen families and improve outcomes for children.

Education

Bachelor's degree in social work, psychology, education, or human services related field OR
An associate's degree with two years of experience working with families is acceptable, provided you are actively working toward a bachelor's degree in human services, social work, education or related field and are to be completed with your degree within six months.

Experience

Experience working with children and families.
Familiarity with child welfare systems, community resources, and protective factors frameworks.

What You'll Bring

You believe in the strength and potential of families—even during difficult circumstances. You are skilled at building trust, engaging people from diverse backgrounds, and helping families navigate challenges while maintaining dignity and hope. You bring knowledge of child welfare and community resources, strong organizational and communication skills, and a willingness to adapt to the needs of families.

Applicants must meet all position requirements, including required screenings, driver's license and car insurance requirements, technology expectations, and the ability to maintain a flexible schedule that supports family needs. Preference will be given to applicants who reside within the assigned service area.

Work Environment

This position involves a combination of work performed from a home office or other designated workspace, along with in-home visits and community outreach. The MFT Advocate travels throughout the assigned service area (Shiawassee and Gratiot counties) with mileage paid, including extended travel for multi-county contracts.

Because families are best served where they live and interact, advocates work in a variety of home and community environments that may include animals, smoke, strong odors, clutter, and insects. Evening, weekend and holiday availability is required in order to consistently meet with families and work with their schedules; you'll have supervisor and team support to manage schedules. The role is subject to frequent interruptions, schedule changes based on family needs and driving in all weather conditions.

Why Join Wellspring?

This role is more than a job. It is an opportunity to help families remain safely together, support parents in creating brighter futures for their children, and be part of a program that is transforming the way services are delivered across Michigan. Every conversation, every visit and every relationship has the potential to create lasting change.

If you believe families deserve hope, support and the opportunity to succeed, this role offers the chance to make a meaningful difference every day.

Apply Today.

Position Title

Program Manager - Regional Hub (THRIVE)

Job Description Summary

The Regional Hub Program Manager serves as the primary regional lead for implementing the Thrive Kansas Digital Mental Health Initiative within an assigned Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) regional hub. This position works closely with healthcare organizations, providers, community health workers, and project leadership to support deployment, adoption and ongoing use of digital mental health services. The role is responsible for coordinating regional activities, facilitating stakeholder engagement, addressing implementation barriers, monitoring progress, and ensuring alignment with project goals, timelines, and quality standards.

The Thrive Kansas Digital Mental Health Initiative is a grant funded, statewide, evidence-based digital therapeutic strategy designed to expand access to treatment for depression, substance use disorders (SUD) and other mental disorders in rural Kansas. The initiative deploys clinically validated computerized mental health interventions supported by community-based facilitation and integrated into rural primary care, behavioral health, and community settings.

We are currently recruiting for three program manager positions.

Job Description

Job Duties

Regional Deployment & Site Readiness

Coordinate regional deployment readiness activities and implementation timelines for participating sites.
Ensure sites complete onboarding, platform setup, workflow preparation, and readiness requirements to support successful implementation.
Serve as the primary regional point of contact during deployment and collaborate with technical teams, providers, and partner organizations to support operational readiness.
Track regional implementation milestones, identify barriers or delays that may affect project objectives, and coordinate resolution of. deployment-related issues with project leadership and technical support teams.

Regional Implementation & Training Coordination

Lead regional implementation activities and coordinate rollout across participating healthcare organizations, community settings, and behavioral health partners in alignment with statewide project plans and timelines.
Support training logistics for providers, CHWs, supervisors, navigators, and support staff, including scheduling, tracking attendance, and ensuring training completion.
Monitor implementation progress across sites and assess adherence to implementation plans and established workflows, identifying and addressing region-specific operational barriers that may affect implementation success.
Facilitate communication between participating sites and project leadership to support successful adoption and sustained use of digital mental health interventions.

Workforce & Program Operations Management

Coordinate workflows among CHWs, supervisors, providers, and care teams across the regional hub.
Support onboarding and integration of newly hired staff and facilitate role clarity among team members.
Monitor workforce capacity, staffing coverage, and continuity across participating sites. Identify workforce challenges or risks and communicate concerns to project leadership in a timely manner.
Promote consistent program operations across sites by documenting workflow processes, facilitating communication among stakeholders, and promoting alignment with project goals and expectations.

Evaluation, Reporting & Continuous Quality Improvement

Coordinate regional participation in program evaluation, performance monitoring, and continuous quality improvement (CQI) activities, ensuring participating sites complete required evaluation activities and data collection requirements.
Track completion of CQI action items and follow-up activities within the region. Support local teams in understanding program performance expectations, implementation benchmarks, and reporting requirements.
Collect and communicate region-specific implementation insights, successes, challenges, and lessons learned to the central evaluation and leadership teams.
Participate in quality improvement meetings and facilitate implementation of approved improvement strategies across participating sites.

End-User Access & Support Coordination

Coordinate regional activities designed to improve access to digital mental health services and interventions.
Monitor barriers to patient, participant, or end-user engagement and enrollment, and collaborate with technical support and program staff to identify, route, and resolve access-related issues.
Track recurring access concerns and communicate trends to project leadership.
Serve as a regional advocate for participating sites and end-users by ensuring barriers affecting engagement, access, or adoption are elevated and addressed in a timely manner.

Stakeholder Engagement & Communication

Serve as the primary regional liaison between participating organizations, project leadership, community partners, and implementation teams.
Facilitate regular meetings with regional stakeholders to review implementation progress, identify challenges, and coordinate solutions.
Maintain ongoing communication regarding project updates, timelines, deliverables, and performance expectations.
Support dissemination of project information and promote engagement among participating organizations and community partners.
Adapt communication strategies to meet the needs of rural healthcare organizations and diverse stakeholder groups.

Integration with Statewide Program Operations

Support alignment between regional implementation activities and statewide project goals.
Coordinate with other Regional Hub Program Managers and central project leadership to ensure consistency across regions.
Share best practices, successful implementation strategies, and lessons learned across regional hubs.
Contribute to statewide planning, implementation meetings, and strategic initiatives designed to strengthen program performance and sustainability.
Conducts activities in a professional and ethical manner, and in accordance with KUMC Policies and applicable local, state and federal laws and regulations.
Performs job responsibilities in a safe and secure manner.

Develops, maintains and expands job-specific knowledge and skills to keep pace with industry changes and supports the university's commitment to excellence and innovation.
Participates in relevant committees, task force, or other similar activities.
Maintain confidentiality of medical center, employee, and patient information. Manages sensitive data with discretion and in accordance with KUMC policies and legal requirements.
Maintains the highest standards of integrity, respect, professional conduct, and ethical standards.
